rows.requirement: Corporate subscribers need no reg-22 consent. Individual subscribers, including sole traders and unincorporated partnerships, need consent or the reg 22(3) soft opt-in. UK GDPR legitimate interests and the absolute Article 21 objection apply to named addresses regardless of subscriber class, so the exemption turns on the recipient's legal form.

source.citation: Privacy and Electronic Communications (EC Directive) Regulations 2003, regs 2, 22

rows.penalty_note: Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 penalty uplift effective 2026-02-05 aligns PECR maxima with UK GDPR.

rows.requirement: Reg 22 electronic mail reaches a platform direct message sent to an individual subscriber's address, so the corporate-versus-individual subscriber distinction governs the platform lane exactly as it governs email. The exemption still turns on the recipient's legal form.

source.citation: ICO direct marketing guidance, electronic mail

rows.penalty_note: Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 penalty uplift effective 2026-02-05 aligns PECR maxima with UK GDPR.

rows.requirement: The sender's identity is never concealed or disguised (reg 23(a)).

rows.penalty_note: Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 penalty uplift effective 2026-02-05 aligns PECR maxima with UK GDPR.

rows.requirement: Every message carries a valid address to which the recipient may send a cease request (reg 23(b)).

rows.penalty_note: Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 penalty uplift effective 2026-02-05 aligns PECR maxima with UK GDPR.

rows.requirement: Opt-in is the default. The published-business-address exemption (Art. 3(1)(iv)) requires three machine-checkable facts about the address: it was published BY the recipient, it was published in the course of business, and no statement refusing marketing was attached to it. A stored address without its publication context cannot evaluate this row.

source.citation: 特定電子メールの送信の適正化等に関する法律 第三条

rows.penalty_note: Spoofed sender information carries a direct criminal penalty; corporate fines apply alongside individual liability.

rows.requirement: The Act is scoped to 特定電子メール (electronic mail). A platform direct message falls outside that scope and outside the published-business-address exemption, so no publication context is available to claim; platform terms govern the lane.

source.citation: 総務省 特定電子メール法 ガイドライン, scope of 特定電子メール

rows.penalty_note: Spoofed sender information carries a direct criminal penalty; corporate fines apply alongside individual liability.

rows.requirement: Directive floor: consent for natural persons, soft opt-in for existing customers on similar products. Legal-person treatment is national, so the floor cannot be applied without knowing the recipient's legal form; where a country row is missing, the strict pole applies.
rows.penalty_note: National transpositions set their own penalties; several member states add private enforcement on top of the supervisory authority.

rows.requirement: The art. 13 floor is technology-neutral for unsolicited direct marketing communications, so a platform direct message inherits the same natural-person consent rule and the same national legal-person question.
rows.penalty_note: National transpositions set their own penalties; several member states add private enforcement on top of the supervisory authority.

rows.requirement: The identity of the sender is never concealed or disguised (art. 13(4)).
rows.penalty_note: National transpositions set their own penalties; several member states add private enforcement on top of the supervisory authority.

rows.requirement: Every message carries a valid address to which the recipient may send a cease request (art. 13(4)).
rows.penalty_note: National transpositions set their own penalties; several member states add private enforcement on top of the supervisory authority.

rows.requirement: The commercial nature of the communication is identifiable as such (art. 13(4) read with e-Commerce Directive art. 6).
rows.penalty_note: National transpositions set their own penalties; several member states add private enforcement on top of the supervisory authority.

rows.requirement: UWG §7 requires prior express opt-in for both B2B and B2C advertising email. There is no business-recipient exemption; double opt-in is the evidentiary standard German courts expect.
rows.penalty_note: Private Abmahnung enforcement makes a single unlawful send actionable by competitors, independent of any supervisory fine.

rows.requirement: UWG §7(1) covers unzumutbare Belästigung by any advertising channel, so a platform direct message carries the same prior-opt-in requirement as email. No business-recipient exemption is available.
rows.penalty_note: Private Abmahnung enforcement makes a single unlawful send actionable by competitors, independent of any supervisory fine.

rows.requirement: Retain the double-opt-in evidence for each address; the sender carries the burden of proving consent. Post-send obligation: retention is enforced by the evidence path, not by the dispatch gate.

source.citation: Gesetz gegen den unlauteren Wettbewerb §7; BGH double-opt-in case law

rows.penalty_note: Private Abmahnung enforcement makes a single unlawful send actionable by competitors, independent of any supervisory fine.

rows.requirement: CPCE L.34-5 with CNIL guidance tolerates B2B opt-out prospection when the message is professionally relevant to the recipient's role, the recipient was informed at collection, and a working opt-out is present. Generic role addresses sit outside the consent regime entirely, so the recipient's legal form decides which branch applies.

source.citation: CNIL, prospection commerciale B2B; Code des postes et des communications électroniques L.34-5

rows.penalty_note: CNIL sanctions under the ePrivacy transposition are assessed independently of the GDPR one-stop-shop.

rows.requirement: CNIL applies the same professional-relevance test to platform direct messages addressed to a professional, so the B2B opt-out branch remains conditional on the recipient's legal form.
rows.penalty_note: CNIL sanctions under the ePrivacy transposition are assessed independently of the GDPR one-stop-shop.

rows.requirement: CAN-SPAM is an opt-out regime: no prior consent is required, and business-to-business email is fully in scope. Federal preemption makes this the single US row set for truthful commercial mail; deception re-activates state statutes.
rows.penalty_note: Up to $53,088 per email (2025 civil-penalty figure, held for 2026); aggravated violations stack.

rows.requirement: CAN-SPAM is scoped to electronic mail messages, so a platform direct message is governed by platform terms and state UDAP law rather than the federal opt-out regime. No prior consent is required by this row.

source.citation: 15 U.S.C. §7702(6) definition of electronic mail message

rows.requirement: Disposition row for an absent or low-confidence jurisdiction. Evaluation proceeds under the strictest seeded pole named by the pack rather than denying automatically, so facts that satisfy that pole allow and a requirement the pole states blocks. This row states the disposition; it never contributes a requirement of its own.
